speaker: Doctor
text: How would you describe the consistency and frequency of your stools, and have you noticed any blood or mucus? Additionally, do you experience significant weight loss or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the relief with defecation and urgency strongly suggest inflammatory bowel disease or infectious colitis. Did you notice any change in the color of your stool, or have you experienced joint pain or eye redness recently? REQUEST TEST: Fecal Calprotectin and Stool Culture.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal calprotectin and culture results, infection and active IBD are unlikely; have you noticed any blood in your stool, or do you experience bloating and flatulence after eating certain foods like dairy or wheat? REQUEST TEST: Celiac_Serology.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since infection, inflammatory bowel disease, and celiac disease have been ruled out, have you noticed any bloating, gas, or discomfort specifically after consuming dairy products or wheat? REQUEST TEST: Lactose_Intolerance and Hydrogen_Breath_Test. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvis_Colonoscopy (if symptoms persist or worsen).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Mucus.
